text:
Melancholy, draw out your sweet beak now;
+
+do not fatten your fasts on my wheatfields of light.
+
+Melancholy, enough! How your daggers drink
+
+the blood my blue leech would draw!
+
+
+Do not finish the manna of woman that has descended;
+
+I want some cross to be born of it tomorrow,
+
+tomorrow, when I have no one toward whom to turn my eyes,
+
+when the coffin opens its great mocking O.
+
+
+My heart is a flowerpot watered with bitterness;
+
+other old birds graze inside it…
+
+Melancholy, stop drying the life from me,
+
+and strip bare your woman’s lip…!

translation.title: Ostrich
translation.editorial_note: The ostrich is never named within the address but survives in melancholy’s beak and devouring fast; the coffin’s O retains its visual and vocal mockery.
